statement: Claude Code 2.1.305 runs the matching hooks of one event at the same time, not one after another.
On Claude Code 2.1.305, a command hook with args runs without a shell.
On Claude Code 2.1.305, a type http hook's additionalContext reaches the model.
Creating a process costs at least four orders of magnitude more than a system call.
Starting a hook through Git Bash costs about 100 ms or more on top of starting it directly.
Every kept-open transport measured (kept-open TCP, HTTP keep-alive, stdio pipe) has p99 under 1 ms and p99.9 under 2 ms on this machine.
A new loopback TCP connection per call adds about 1 ms at p50 over a kept-open one.
The differences between kept-open transports are under 1 ms at p99.9, far below the cost of starting one process.
On this machine, Nagle and delayed ACK cause no 40 to 200 ms stall on loopback.
Most of the measured 7 ms host.connect is not the TCP connect.
The X host refuses a request larger than 64 KiB because of asyncio's default readline limit.
A host started as the child of one MCP server cannot be the single host per account shared by every Claude session.
A long computation or blocking call inside a single event loop stalls every request it serves.
The MCP proxy walks the source tree synchronously before relaying each tool call.
Python asyncio's default Windows event loop does not support a Unix-socket server.
Windows creates every new process with a fresh address space built from scratch rather than by forking an existing process. (lecture: windowsInternals)
Before a Windows program's main runs, the loader maps its imported DLLs recursively and runs their DllMain and TLS callbacks under the loader lock. (lecture: windowsInternals)
In the Cygwin benchmark, 1,000 forks took about 0.23 s on native Linux and 10 to 16 s under Cygwin on Windows. (lecture: cygwinFork)
Raising cygserver thread counts, changing the power plan and debloating Windows cut Cygwin's fork time by more than half. (lecture: cygwinFork)
In a single-threaded event-loop server, one handler that blocks on I/O stalls every other client. (lecture: dahlNode)
Node resolves host names through the operating system resolver on its worker thread pool, while network sockets are polled directly by the event loop. (lecture: belderEventLoop)
When a middlebox drops its state for an idle TCP connection, both peers are notified at once. (lecture: nasserKeepAlive)
HTTP has a request header with which the client tells the server how long to keep the connection alive. (lecture: nasserKeepAlive)
When the last writer of a pipe closes, the reader gets end-of-file, and when the last reader closes, a writer gets SIGPIPE or EPIPE. (lecture: cs162Ipc)
inotify reports events by watch descriptor, and the application itself must keep and update the descriptor-to-path mapping, including on renames. (lecture: inotify)
Hedged requests are appropriate for mutating requests as long as each request is cheap. (lecture: tailAtScale)
The more machines a single request touches, the higher the chance it hits at least one slow machine. (lecture: tailAtScale)
Response time stays roughly flat until utilisation approaches 100%. (lecture: thompsonPerformance)
Node cut its startup from about 60 ms to about 21 ms mainly through lazy loading, a code cache and a V8 startup snapshot. (lecture: cheungNodeStartup)
